subject.title: [Feature]: Network Access Control (allowedDomains / denyDomains) — Egress Firewall

question: Should OpenClaw expose local web-tool domain allow/deny config, defer egress policy to a managed proxy/external controls, or start with a scoped web_fetch hostnameAllowlist contract?
rationale: This is a public security/config boundary and the open implementation paths make different product and security guarantees that automation should not choose without maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve Scoped web_fetch First
options.body: Review and sponsor the narrow web_fetch hostnameAllowlist path as an interim contract while tracking denied domains, managed search, browser, and proxy coverage separately.

options.title: Design Shared Egress Policy
options.body: Pause narrow local knobs and define one cross-tool contract for fetch, search, browser, providers, redirects, caches, and proxy routing before implementation lands.

options.title: Use Managed Proxy Boundary
options.body: Route application-owned egress policy through proxy.enabled and external operator policy instead of adding a local domain firewall to web tools.

recommendation.title: Approve Scoped web_fetch First
recommendation.body: Review and sponsor the narrow web_fetch hostnameAllowlist path as an interim contract while tracking denied domains, managed search, browser, and proxy coverage separately.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent overlap across SSRF/net policy history and the active web_fetch hostname allowlist PR.
